NEW DELHI: Be it sport or society, the participation of youth is India’s strength, PM Narendra Modi said Thursday, calling upon them to take to sports at a time when more avenues have emerged for their participation.Speaking at the Khelo India dialogue, he said, “More important than screens are sports centres. More important than PlayStation is the playground. And this will happen only when the youth embrace this approach.” Lamenting India’s absence from almost half of Olympic sports, he said that is why he had announced a talent hunt for children in the 5-15 years age bracket.“In the 2012 Olympics, India participated in only 13 sports. In more than 20 disciplines, India had no presence.” Indian sportspersons must achieve mastery in these disciplines to increase the medal tally, Modi said, noting that the country’s vast coastline and mountainous regions should help produce sportspersons who are into surfing and sport climbing.No Indian has ever competed in these disciplines at the Olympics. Both are part of 2028 Olympics. “We have both the demography and geography for water sports and winter sports.Yet we are not visible in such sports globally.”With India keen to host 2036 Olympics, he said, “Our focus should be on preparing sportspersons who will qualify and compete in different sports in 2036.” Referring to his Independence Day address where he spoke about boosting the sporting ecosystem, he said this should not be confined to winning medals but must be a campaign to integrate youth power with sporting power.

Sriram Kartik sweeps 10 awards including the ‘Best Junior contestant’ across Carnatic vocal and mrudangam; prizes presented by eminent Vidwan Sikkil Gurucharan on 23 Aug 2026 in MumbaiA fifteen-year-old from Powai has won ten awards at the Music Competition 2026 conducted by Sri Shanmukhananda Bharatiya Sangeetha Vidyalaya and Natya Vidyalaya, competing in both Carnatic vocal and mrudangam.Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of Shanmukhananda's Carnataka Sangeetha Pon Mazhai Thiruvizha, at the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha in Matunga. The prizes were presented by Shanmukha Sangeetha Shiromani Vidwan Shri Sikkil Gurucharan, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, who presided over the ceremony.Vidwan Sikkil C Gurucharan is a leading Indian Carnatic classical vocalist and youth ambassador for the art form. A singer born into a family of flautists, and grandson of Sikkil Kunjumani, the elder of the Sikkil Sisters, he trained under B Krishnamurthy and Vaigal S. Gnanaskandan, himself a disciple of Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and gave his first concert at The Music Academy, Chennai at the age of twelve. Recipient of the Kalaimamani award from the Tamil Nadu government in 2020, Sikkil C Gurucharan has been featured by India Today as one of the 35 Game Changers Under 35 in India.Sriram Kartik won 9 individual prizes — five first prizes, three seconds and one third. He was also awarded a cash prize for being the Best Junior contestant winning the maximum number of prizes in the 10-to-15 years age category.The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla. It drew more than 300 participants from across India and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.Sriram's two mrudangam prizes came in the only two categories open to his age group — a first for tani avartanam in roopakam and misra chapu talams, and a second for adi talam with five jathi mohras, awarded under the TS Nandakumar's Percussive Arts Centre Endowment and the Guru TS Nandakumar Endowment respectively.His seven vocal prizes spanned first places in compositions of the Trinity, varnams, Purandaradasa kritis; the Silver Lamp Prize for keertanams and kritis; second places in Subramania Bharatiyar compositions and Tamizh compositions; and a third in GNB kritis.Every prize at Shanmukhananda is attached to an endowment instituted in the name of an artist, a patron or an institution. He won awards under the following endowments namely - GNB Endowment, the Kalki Memorial, the Dr S Pinakapani Endowment, the BVS Iyengar Memorial and the Lakshmi Gopalakrishna Memorial. The Best Junior award came under the Smt. Parvathy Subramaniam Endowment and S Ramakrishnan Memorial.Sriram began learning the mrudangam at the age of five, under Acharya Ratna Vidwan Mumbai Shri Shankaranarayanan at Powai Fine Arts. A decade on, he has kept at it through the school years in which most students of classical music quietly stop — the age at which coaching classes, board examinations and the ordinary pull of everything else tend to close the practice room door for good.Sustaining it alongside school is the part a prize list does not show. Practice sessions run two and a half to three hours. Nine vocal categories at 5-6 compositions a piece meant something close to 45-50 pieces in which he participated of which he won prizes across seven categories, readied to a standard that would survive a judging panel, with two percussion categories besides.He now receives higher tutelage in mrudangam from Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Academi Awardee Vidwan Dr Umayalpuram K Sivaraman, and trains in Carnatic vocal music under Acharya Ratnakara Vidwan Sherthalai Dr KN Renganatha Sharma and Vidushi Dr Mohana Sharma. He holds a CCRT Scholarship for Mrudangam from the ministry of culture, and presented his mrudangam arangetram in June last year, the day after his fourteenth birthday.
Article Summary: Sriram kartik received awards at prize distribution ceremony held on sunday (aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of shanmukhananda's carnataka sangeetha pon mazhai thiruvizha. The competition drew more than 300 participants from across india and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.

Article Title: Could Frederik Andersen’s injury disrupt the Edmonton Oilers’ NHL goaltending plans before the 2026 season
Article Text:
Frederik Andersen #31 raises the Stanley Cup during the Carolina Hurricanes Stanley Cup Final Victory Parade on June 20, 2026 at Downtown Raleigh,.(Photo by Jaylynn Nash/Getty Images)

How will Frederik Andersen’s injury affect Edmonton Oilers NHL goaltending plans?

What is known about Frederik Andersen’s injury?

Why does Andersen’s absence matter for the NHL season?

Edmonton Oilers enter training camp with question marks around Frederik Andersen after the veteran netminder was injured during offseason training. The team announced Andersen’s injury but did not disclose its severity and said he is not expected to be ready for the start of camp.After helping the Carolina Hurricanes win the Stanley Cup, Andersen signed a one-year, $2.8 million deal with the Edmonton Oilers. His loss is a big one because Edmonton brought him in to provide experience and stability to a goaltending position that was a struggle last season.The Edmonton Oilers could be forced to lean more on their backup options in goal while they await an update on Frederik Andersen’s availability due to injury.The Edmonton Oilers bolstered a key area of weakness by signing Frederik Andersen. The Danish goalie, 36, played in the NHL for 13 seasons with the Anaheim Ducks, Toronto Maple Leafs and Carolina Hurricanes.In the 2025-26 regular season, Andersen had a.874 save percentage and a 3.05 goals-against average in 35 starts for the Carolina Hurricanes. His numbers weren't spectacular, but he was noticeably better in the playoffs.During the Hurricanes’ run to the Stanley Cup, Andersen was 13-2 with a 1.89 goals-against average.910 save percentage and three shutouts in 16 games. That playoff experience was a big reason Edmonton liked him.The Edmonton Oilers did not divulge the type of injury Frederik Andersen sustained in the offseason or how serious it is. The team has also not set a timetable for his return.That uncertainty makes his status particularly important with training camp approaching. Edmonton said another update will come when appropriate, leaving the team and its fans with no clear indication whether Andersen might be back early in the season.With Andersen out of training camp, the expectation is that goalies Tristan Jarry and Devon Levi will get a few extra looks from the Edmonton Oilers.Andersen is out of action, so this could be an opportunity for Jarry to take on a bigger role. Meanwhile, Levi would get valuable NHL exposure if Edmonton handles its crease well through camp and the preseason.The vacancy also provides the organization an opportunity to test its depth before making any further decisions.Timing is particularly important as Edmonton was already looking to get better in net. The Oilers ended last season with a .883 team save percentage, which was among the worst in the NHL.Edmonton’s training camp opens Sept. 16, and the Oilers face the Winnipeg Jets in their first pre-season game on Sept. 19. The Oilers open the regular season on September 29 against the Vancouver Canucks.If Andersen is healthy enough to stay on the sideline into the regular season, Edmonton could be under immediate pressure to find a reliable answer in net. His eventual return could be one of the key storylines early in the season for the Oilers.
Article Summary: Frederik andersen signed a one-year, $2.8 million deal with the edmonton oilers. The team announced andersen’s injury but did not disclose its severity and said he is not expected to be ready for the start of camp. Tristan jarry and devon levi will get a few extra looks from the oilers.

Article Title: "The toughest part is trusting your body": NFL analyst raises concerns over Patrick Mahomes' confidence ahead of return
Article Text:

Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, is eyeing a return in the new season even as concerns about his injuries have only grown in the last few days. With the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player missing the two preseason games, there have been doubts about his recovery. Amid this, NFL analyst Geoff Schwartz has weighed in on Patrick Mahomes.A few hours ago, popular NFL analyst Geoff Schwartz made an appearance on First Things First where he opened up about Patrick Mahomes’ confidence.NFL analyst Geoff Schwartz said, “Just trust and confidence, right? When you're coming back from injury, that's the toughest part as a player is trusting your body to do the same things you did previously…”NFL analyst Geoff Schwartz added, “'You have to make that first throw when someone's around his legs, how does he do that with confidence, right? How do you not have a flashback to the bad things that happen?”Back on Tuesday, in an interview with ESPN, Patrick Mahomes opened up about his recovery as he said, “It’s nine months…”The Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback added, “It’s the amount of time [doctors] said from the beginning, that if I did everything the right way, I would be ready to play Week One.”Patrick Mahomes continued, “I’m someone that, if you put [a goal] out in front of me, I want to go out and get it and maximize every single opportunity, every rep in the weight room, every hour that I can spend in the building to get my body right.”While Patrick Mahomes did seem to miss the preseason matches, he has been pretty regular at training camps.Despite the constant assurances by the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes, there have been doubts among fans.With just days left for the Kansas City Chiefs’ season opener against the Denver Broncos, the team has been struggling with a number of injuries.As Patrick Mahomes’ situation remains stressful, the list of players who have missed practices recently have only grown in the last few days.This includes Kenneth Walker, Josh Simmons, Chamarri Conner, Ashton Gillotte, Alohi Gilman, Jack Cochrane, C.J. Hanson, Jimmy Holiday, Tyreke Smith, and Chris Oladokun.However, the Kansas City Chiefs’ head coach Andy Reid remains confident about his team as they eye a Super Bowl after losing it in 2025 against the Philadelphia Eagles.The last season seemed to be a brutal one for the team as they recorded just 6 wins and 11 losses. It was also the first time since 2014 that the team ended up missing the playoffs and was ruled out of it.

Auston Matthews #34 of the Toronto Maple Leafs warms up before playing against the Anaheim Ducks at the Scotiabank Arena on March 12, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (Photo by Mark Blinch/NHLI via Getty Images)

Why could Auston Matthews miss TSN’s NHL top 10?

Frank Corrado questions Matthews’ current NHL status

Auston Matthews’ tough 2025-26 season with the Toronto Maple Leafs has made talk of whether he will remain inside the top 10 in the NHL a talking point. TSN’s Bryan Hayes and Frank Corrado were talking recently about where the star center might land in the network’s upcoming player rankings, and Corrado was especially skeptical.The debate follows NHL Network ranking Matthews No. 8 on its list of the top 20 centers. That ranking also had Montreal Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki ninth with 101 points and a Selke Trophy win, adding to the debate about where Matthews stands right now.The biggest issue is Matthews’ recent production and availability. Frank Corrado believes Matthews could drop out of TSN’s top 10, while Bryan Hayes also questioned whether the Toronto Maple Leafs captain is currently worthy of a spot in the top 15 players in the league.Matthews finished the 2025-26 season with 27 goals and 53 points in 60 games, the lowest totals of his 10-season NHL career. He was injured for 22 games, but still became the all-time goal-scoring leader of the Toronto Maple Leafs.That drop is especially significant because Matthews had become one of the NHL’s top goal scorers. Before last season, he had scored at least 30 goals in each of the previous nine seasons.Corrado already has Matthews outside the top 10, which means the center could fall somewhere in the No.17-to-25 range in TSN’s upcoming ranking. His view is less about Matthews’ career to date than his recent form.Matthews could fall out of the top 10 due to the way he has played over the last two seasons, Hayes argued. Where Matthews ends up on TSN's new Top 50 list is a mystery, as it has yet to be released.Matthews’ ranking by the NHL Network has also drawn comparisons to Nick Suzuki. Suzuki finished with 101 points in 82 games, won the Selke Trophy and helped the Canadiens reach the Eastern Conference Final.Matthews was eighth, and Suzuki was ninth among centers. Matthews’ standing as one of the NHL’s best has grown increasingly uncertain heading into the new season, following the gap in 2025-26 results.So the upcoming TSN ranking could be an important indicator of how NHL analysts view Matthews’ standing after a campaign cut short by injury.Auston Matthews’ status among the NHL’s best players is being challenged ahead of TSN’s upcoming Top 50 ranking. The Toronto Maple Leafs captain recorded 53 points in 60 games before his 2025-26 season ended due to injury. Analysts Bryan Hayes and Frank Corrado can't agree if Matthews still deserves a top-10 spot going into the 2026-27 season.

Article Title: What’s going on with Kyle Singler? 6-foot-8 ex-Thunder star posts disturbing video about Coach K
Article Text:
Kyle Singler. Image via: Cooper Neill/ Getty Images file

What's going on with Kyle Singler?

What did Kyle Singler say about Coach K?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kyle Singler is at the center of a troubling story after the former Duke standout posted a string of rambling Instagram videos this week, aiming pointed accusations at his old college coach, Mike Krzyzewski. The clips show him pacing through what looks like an empty house, insisting people are trying to hurt him and take his money.It's a jarring turn for a guy once known for hitting big shots on college basketball's biggest stage. Now the questions aren't about his jumper. They're about his safety.The videos surfaced on Tuesday night, and they don't look good. Kyle Singler, 38, wanders from room to room, appears to be agitated, describing a life that sounds nothing like the one he built during his NBA years. He says his power has been shut off. He says his house has been broken into. He says money is being drained from accounts he can barely track anymore.None of that has been independently verified. But the pattern is familiar to anyone who followed his last public flare-up. Back in November 2024, Singler posted something similar, telling followers he feared for his life every single day. This week's videos pick up roughly where that one left off, only louder and more disjointed.There's also history sitting underneath all of this. Singler was arrested in Oklahoma last October after his girlfriend told police he grabbed her by the head and shoved her to the ground during an argument at an Airbnb, with their child present. He posted bond on a misdemeanor charge and the case has largely stayed out of headlines since, until now.Singler didn't just vent about strangers or unnamed enemies. He went after Krzyzewski directly, the coach who guided him to a national title in 2010 and later called him one of the most complete players he'd ever developed.Singler claims he reached out for help and got nothing back. "Coach K has set me up, man," he said in one clip, adding that Krzyzewski had "fully dismissed" his messages.“You guys are cutting my power off, breaking into my house, stealing money, ruining my life. I reached out to Coach K and all he did was sit me on the bench. Thanks, man. Is that what we're doing at that school, sitting people down, teaching them up? Cool beans, man.Coach, where you at? Help a brother out. Thought we were on the same team, man," Singler shared.He described feeling abandoned by the program he once helped define, at one point comparing his situation to being benched, as though the man who shaped his career had simply stopped answering the phone.It's worth remembering where Singler came from. He was the engine of Duke's 2010 championship run, earned Most Outstanding Player honors in that tournament, and went on to play seven NBA seasons split between Detroit and Oklahoma City after going 33rd overall in 2011. He pulled in more than $22 million over his career, most of it from a contract extension with the Thunder.
Article Summary: Former duke star kyle singler posted a string of rambling instagram videos this week. The clips show him pacing through what looks like an empty house, insisting people are trying to hurt him and take his money. Singler claims he reached out for help and got nothing back from his old coach, mike krzyzewski.

Article Title: Kieron Pollard surpasses Jos Buttler, reclaims world record for most runs in T20 cricket
Article Text:

Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard has become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket after going past England batter Jos Buttler 's tally during the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) 2026.Pollard entered the record books on Thursday when he scored 65 off 26 balls for Trinbago Knight Riders against Saint Lucia Kings at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba.The former Mumbai Indians player needed 35 runs before the match to move past Buttler, who had 14,890 T20 runs.Earlier this year, Pollard had overtaken Chris Gayle to become the highest run-scorer in T20 cricket. Buttler then moved ahead of him in August 2026 while playing for Manchester Super Giants in The Hundred. Pollard has now reclaimed the top spot.The 39-year-old now has 14,921 runs from 666 innings in 749 T20 matches.Pollard will get a chance to become the first player to score 15,000 runs in T20 cricket when Trinbago Knight Riders face Barbados Tridents at the same venue on Friday (Saturday IST).His innings came at a strike rate of 250 and included six fours and five sixes while chasing a target of 212 for the Andre Russell-led Trinbago Knight Riders.The five sixes also took Pollard's career tally to 1,010 sixes in T20 cricket. He is now 47 sixes away from Chris Gayle's record for the most sixes in the format.Pollard and Gayle are the only players to hit more than 1,000 sixes in T20 cricket. Andre Russell is third on the list with 808 sixes.

The 39-year-old scored 65 off 26 balls for trinbago knight riders against saint lucia kings at the brian lara stadium in tarouba. The former mumbai indians player needed 35 runs before the match to move past england batter jos buttler.

Article Title: After 75 years the Pro Bowl is dead: Here's what replaces the game nobody wanted to watch
Article Text:
NFL ends the Pro Bowl game after 75 years (Via X)

Why did the NFL cancel the Pro Bowl game?

What happens to the Pro Bowl now that the game is gone?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL officially ended the Pro Bowl game on Wednesday, closing out a 75-year tradition that had slowly lost the plot. The league announced at its owners meeting in Atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as Pro Bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in Los Angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone. This is not a pause. The NFL is not regrouping. It is a full stop on what had become the most skippable event on the sports calendar.The honest answer is that the players stopped caring, and the league finally admitted it out loud. NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent spoke directly with more than a dozen star players this summer, and what he heard was consistent. They did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. Vincent put it plainly at the owners meeting: "You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that. Frankly, it just doesn't sit well. This isn't a good representation."That admission matters more than it might seem. For years the NFL kept pushing the format, hoping a tweak would fix the problem.The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades. In 2023 the league switched entirely to flag football, hoping the casual format would generate energy. It did not. Ratings stayed soft. Players showed up out of obligation, not excitement. Nobody was fooled.Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president overseeing events, framed the decision with uncommon directness. "It's OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game," he said in Atlanta. That line will not make headlines for its poetry, but it signals something real: the NFL is no longer interested in defending a product it cannot fix.The title survives. The game does not. The NFL confirmed that 88 players will still earn Pro Bowl recognition after this season and be honored at an event in Los Angeles. Several flag football exhibitions will take place around that time, though they will serve as entertainment rather than competition. The core distinction, being named one of the best at your position in the NFL, stays intact.The league also eliminated replacement selections going forward. In the past, injured players or Super Bowl participants were swapped out for alternates, which diluted the honor. Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Shedeur Sanders made the Pro Bowl this year as a replacement. Under the new structure, that category is gone. If a player earns it, they earn it outright.O'Reilly explained the thinking behind the restructured honor: "The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL. A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."The voting process stays the same: an equal split between players, coaches, and fans. What changes is the weight behind it. Without a game to water things down, a Pro Bowl selection becomes a cleaner acknowledgment of a great season rather than a footnote to an event most people forgot was happening.
Article Summary: Nfl ends the pro bowl game after 75 years. The league announced at its owners meeting in atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as pro bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in los angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I almost died after giving birth to my daughter.” - How Serena Williams turned life-threatening motherhood and family strength into sporting resilience
Article Text:
Serena Williams makes Cincinnati return with Venus after ‘emotional’ family moment with daughters Olympia and Adira

How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.

How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recovery

How did Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. become Serena Williams’ motivation

Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams’ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.Serena’s pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs.She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serena’s intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.“I almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunate… When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.”The CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.For Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serena’s 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.Olympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.“Olympia, does mama look good out here? You’re the reason I’m here, you’re my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. It’s okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.”That message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.By 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an “evolution.”Her decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympia’s wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.“I have never liked the word retirement… Maybe the best word to describe what I’m up to is evolution. I’m here to tell you that I’m evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to me… My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.”Vogue published Serena’s essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serena’s tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympia’s birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.
Article Summary: Serena williams almost died after giving birth to her daughter, alexis olympia ohanian jr. an emergency c-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight grand slam finals.

Article Title: "I’ve sacrificed a lot": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' director Kelli Finglass confronts the possibility of walking away from the America's Sweetheart
Article Text:
America’s Sweethearts

Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticism

Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Kelli Finglass , leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflix’sreturns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.“The words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting...Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. I’m trusting humanity to help figure this one out because it’s a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”That outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected “aha” for me—for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.”..Now entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma…I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”For now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.
Article Summary: Kelli finglass performed for the cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances. Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.

Article Title: Prasidh Krishna reveals his definition of aggression: 'It's about what I'm doing'
Article Text:

‘50% of the job is taking it’

NEW DELHI: Every fast bowler has his own way of showing aggression. Some try to unsettle batters with eye contact, some stay calm, others rely on yorkers, constant appeals or words. India pacer Prasidh Krishna has a different approach - he believes his aggression is best shown through his bowling.Krishna credited disciplined bowling, strong fielding and an attacking mindset for India’s early success against Sri Lanka. The hosts were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended Day Two of the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground on Monday. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.The bowlers had only a short window to work with, but Krishna made it count, picking up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over.Krishna said aggression is not necessarily about showing emotion or getting into a verbal battle with the opposition.“Yeah, I would like to say so. I mean, aggression can come out in different ways, and for me it is about what I'm doing when I'm bowling. It's very easy for people to get away or be distracted by what's happening in the pitch.There's too much happening, there's not too much happening, but I think the focus is still to come in and bowl those areas with full effort,” Krishna told the broadcasters before the start of Day 3’s play.Krishna bowled back of a length outside off and found enough movement from the surface to trouble Lahiru Udara. The Sri Lankan opener edged towards gully, where Yashasvi Jaiswal completed an excellent diving catch to dismiss him for one.Krishna said the wicket was a result of both the conditions and Jaiswal’s fielding effort.“Yeah, I think it was, there’s something in the pitch, of course. Maybe stopped a little bit. There was a bit of seam, and I think credit goes to Jaiswal for the catch that he took. It was an exceptional one. We have been putting in some effort on the field in practice, so I think it just paid off,” he mentioned.India had very little time to bowl before bad light stopped play. Manav Suthar then dismissed Prabath Jayasuriya for two with the final delivery of the day, leaving Sri Lanka at 8/2.Krishna stressed that creating chances is only half the job and the fielders also need to complete the opportunity.“100%. I think 50% of the job is bowling the ball there, getting an edge, but 50% is taking it as well, and we have been pretty good at doing that. I think it's also doing the simple things right, which we have been doing well, and that's what shows,” he added.Krishna also spoke about the need to adjust his length according to the pitch. He said the Indian coaching and analysis staff work together to decide the right approach for each surface.“Length is something that keeps changing with pitches that we play on. So we sit with analysts, coaches, and everything and decide on what's the kind of length that we want to be bowling on different surfaces. And yeah, natural length was something that I could say when I was not playing for the country, but when I'm here I need to be bowling every length that the team wants, and I'm trying to do that,” he concluded.
Article Summary: India bowler prasidh krishna believes aggression is best shown through his bowling. Krishna picked up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over. Sri lanka were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended day two. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from devdutt padikkal and dhruv jurel.

The 2025-26 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship will end in London this weekend, with Rounds 16 and 17 taking place at Excel London on August 15 and 16. While the title battle is expected to be closely fought, sustainability will also be a major focus at the 2026 Hankook London E-Prix. The event is not only about the final two races of the Formula E season. Its sustainability efforts cover energy, waste, food packaging, community projects, education and opportunities for young people.As the championship reaches its season finale, the London E-Prix aims to show how electric racing can combine competition with efforts focused on sustainability and community impact.The London E-Prix will run on 100% certified renewable mains electricity, supported by solar power generated from Excel London’s eco-friendly extension. Track lighting and buffer zones will use dedicated battery storage systems. This will help eliminate the need for continuous generator use. Any remaining emissions will be fully offset.The event will follow a strict zero-waste-to-landfill policy. Non-hazardous waste will be sent for high-rate recycling. Surplus food waste will be composted on-site using commercial wormeries. Used cooking oil will be recycled into biofuel to power plant and machinery.Materials that cannot be recycled will be converted into clean energy.ID@undefinedCaption not available.Food concessions at the 2026 Hankook London E-Prix will use packaging from Notpla, a fellow B Corp-certified brand.The packaging is made from seaweed and natural plant extracts and is home-compostable. It will replace single-use plastics across catering operations and support a circular economy.Mobile provider giffgaff has joined Formula E as the championship's first-ever B Corp partner.The partnership will support the €25,000 Better Futures Fund initiative with Big Issue Recruit. The project will help 20 young Londoners facing employment barriers through one-on-one coaching, barrier-removal grants, refurbished smartphones with data and paid work placements during London E-Prix race week.Formula E and PIF have relaunched the Driving Force platform, which has already engaged more than 94,000 students globally.The platform uses gamified STEM learning based around the next-generation GEN4 car. It also includes trackside workshops during race week and aims to inspire young people to become future leaders in motorsport and sustainability.Formula E's Community Tour will give more than 380 local residents access to the event through two dedicated sessions.The programme brings together more than 15 community, diversity and youth organisations. It includes career-focused sessions for young adults and track tours for local charity beneficiaries, giving underrepresented groups behind-the-scenes access to electric racing.The FIA Girls on Track programme will return to London, with 150 young women aged 12 to 18 taking part.The programme will offer career panels, garage tours, simulator access and discussions on tackling online cyberbullying in sport. It is supported by Hankook, Motorsport UK and Greenpower.Each participant will also receive four race-day tickets, while eight selected participants will take part in the podium ceremony.Also read: 2026 London E-Prix schedule: Round 16 and 17 timings, how to watch Formula E Championship finale and more

Food concessions will use packaging made from seaweed and natural plant extracts. Mobile provider giffgaff has joined formula e as the championship's first-ever b corp partner.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: Final Fantasy Resonance is bringing the series its first HD-2D treatment; Square Enix reveals new characters and a world powered by crystals
Article Text:
Image credit: Square Enix

Final Fantasy Resonance brings HD-2D to a crystal-powered world

Final Fantasy Resonance introduces Jake and Sakura

Final Fantasy Resonance is bringing the series its first HD-2D treatment, combining 2D pixel art with three-dimensional environments and dynamic lighting effects. Square Enix has now shared new details about the turn-based RPG ahead of its October launch, including its crystal-powered world and two new characters, Jake and Sakura.The game marks the first time a Final Fantasy title has used the HD-2D style, introduced with 2018's Octopath Traveller. Resonance is based on the first season of the 2016 mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius. Still, Square Enix says the new version expands and enhances that story rather than simply porting the original game.Resonance takes place in a world where crystals power several nations, while familiar elements from the SNES-era Final Fantasy games return, including chocobos, espers and airships.One of the game's nations is the Zoldaad Empire, a military power built around the fire crystal. According to Square Enix, the empire has mass-produced airships and magitek weaponry and is reportedly planning to use them to invade neighbouring countries.The game will also feature Mysidia, an advanced magical city associated with the Ice Crystal, which is said to exist only in legend. The name will be familiar to Final Fantasy fans, as Mysidia was also the name of a city inhabited by mages in Final Fantasy IV.Zoldaad and Mysidia are also connected to two of the game's new main characters, Jake and Sakura. Square Enix describes Jake as the leader of the rebel army fighting the Zoldaad Empire. While he is presented as someone who can be easily distracted, the company says he is committed to his fellow citizens and determined to end their suffering under the empire.In combat, Jake uses abilities based on chance, including Coin Toss and Gamble Shot.
